system_prompt:
You are taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in the eighth grade. Answer each question as well as you can.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 2 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

Popularity of Subjects

A group of 10 students wanted to find out whether mathematics or history was more popular for their group. They rated each subject using the following scale.

[Image: Rating scale from 1 to 5]

The table shows the results:

Students’ Ratings

| Student | Mathematics Rating | History Rating |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alan | 1 | 2 |
| Lisa | 4 | 4 |
| Ann | 5 | 4 |
| John | 2 | 2 |
| Connor | 4 | 2 |
| Georgia | 3 | 3 |
| Bret | 2 | 1 |
| Courtney | 1 | 1 |
| Ian | 5 | 3 |
| Jackson | 3 | 2 |
| Totals | 30 | 24 |

A. Calculate the mean (average) rating for each subject.

Mean rating for mathematics = ____

Mean rating for history = ____

According to the ratings, which is the more popular subject for this group of students?

More popular subject: ____

Figure, described in words:
A horizontal rating scale shown as a line with 5 equally spaced circular points labeled 1 through 5 above the line. Under each number is a description:
- 1: "Dislike a lot"
- 2: "Dislike"
- 3: "Neither dislike nor like"
- 4: "Like"
- 5: "Like a lot"

## Question 2

Popularity of Subjects

A group of 10 students wanted to find out whether mathematics or history was more popular for their group. They rated each subject using the following scale.

[Image: Rating scale from 1 to 5]

The table shows the results:

Students’ Ratings

| Student | Mathematics Rating | History Rating |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Alan | 1 | 2 |
| Lisa | 4 | 4 |
| Ann | 5 | 4 |
| John | 2 | 2 |
| Connor | 4 | 2 |
| Georgia | 3 | 3 |
| Bret | 2 | 1 |
| Courtney | 1 | 1 |
| Ian | 5 | 3 |
| Jackson | 3 | 2 |
| Totals | 30 | 24 |

B. The students’ ratings are shown on the graph below. For example, Alan’s name is by his ratings (mathematics 1, history 2).

[Image: Scatter plot showing students' ratings]

Write True or False in the space after each of these statements:

All students in the group liked mathematics more than they liked history. ____

Nearly half of the students gave both subjects the same rating. ____

Two students neither liked nor disliked either subject. ____

Figure, described in words:
The item includes two figures:
1. A horizontal rating scale line with 5 marked points labeled 1 through 5, with descriptions below:
- 1: "Dislike a lot"
- 2: "Dislike"
- 3: "Neither dislike nor like"
- 4: "Like"
- 5: "Like a lot"

2. A scatter plot on a 5 by 5 grid:
- Horizontal axis is labeled "Mathematics Rating" with integer markings from 0 to 5.
- Vertical axis is labeled "History Rating" with integer markings from 1 to 5 (origin at 0).
- Plotted points (black dots) with student names next to them:
  - Courtney at (1, 1)
  - Bret at (2, 1)
  - Alan at (1, 2)
  - John at (2, 2)
  - Jackson at (3, 2)
  - Connor at (4, 2)
  - Georgia at (3, 3)
  - Ian at (5, 3)
  - Lisa at (4, 4)
  - Ann at (5, 4)

Answer each of the 2 questions.

answer_1.description: Your answer to question 1, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_1.title: Answer 1

answer_2.description: Your answer to question 2, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer_2.title: Answer 2

output.answer_1: Mean rating for mathematics = 30 ÷ 10 = 3. Mean rating for history = 24 ÷ 10 = 2.4. More popular subject: Mathematics (its mean rating of 3 is higher than history's mean rating of 2.4).
output.answer_2: All students in the group liked mathematics more than they liked history. False (Alan, Georgia? no; e.g., Connor, Ian, Bret and others: Alan rated both 1 and 2 — Alan rated history higher than mathematics, so not all students preferred mathematics). Nearly half of the students gave both subjects the same rating. True (Courtney 1-1, John 2-2, Georgia 3-3, Lisa 4-4 = 4 of 10 students, which is nearly half of the students). Two students neither liked nor disliked either subject. False (only Georgia rated both subjects 3, i.e. neither dislike nor like).
